ozet: Starting from the notice board of Knowledge Harbor, Piko explains the structure of HTML and how to collect titles, links and text with BeautifulSoup.

giris.anlatim: Day 22: Web scraping! In this lesson you'll learn how HTML is built, and collect titles, links and text from pages with BeautifulSoup.

Learn Python step by step in 30 days

sahneler.anlatim: Hi, I'm Piko! The notice board at Knowledge Harbor is full of notices: ship times, prices, lost items. Copying them all into a notebook by hand would take hours. Web pages are boards like this too. Today we learn to collect information from pages: web scraping!
Web pages are written in HTML. Content is marked with tags: h1 is a heading, p is a paragraph, and a is a link. class and href are the tag's attributes, and the words between the tags are the text.

ekran.kod:
Title

25 gold

Go to the map

sahneler.anlatim: BeautifulSoup reads HTML and lets us search inside it. soup.title gets the title, find gets the first matching tag, and find_all brings them all back as a list. The .text at the end gives the words inside the tag.

ekran.kod:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """Harbor Board

Today's ships

Seagull leaves at 10:00.

Dolphin arrives at 14:30.

""" soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") print(soup.title.text) print(soup.find("h1").text) for p in soup.find_all("p"): print("-", p.text)
ekran.cikti:

Today's ships

sahneler.anlatim: To get an attribute's value, I treat the tag like a dictionary: href inside square brackets. Each link's text and address come out side by side.

ekran.kod: from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = 'Map Ships' soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") for a in soup.find_all("a"): print(a.text, "->", a["href"])

sahneler.anlatim: I only want the prices. Since class is a special word in Python, I put an underscore after it. I turn the text I find into numbers with int and add them up.

ekran.kod:
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup html = """
  • Rope 5
  • Lantern 40
    • """ soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser") spans = soup.find_all("span", class_="price") prices = [int(s.text) for s in spans] print(prices, "total:", sum(prices))

sahneler.anlatim: A common mistake: searching for a tag that isn't on the page. If find doesn't find anything, it returns None. Since None has no text, you get an AttributeError. Check whether the result is None first.

sahneler.anlatim: On a real site, the HTML is first downloaded from the internet with requests. But be a polite scraper: check whether the site allows it, don't flood the server with requests, and don't collect personal information. If the site offers an API, use that.

maddeler: If there's an API, use it

sahneler.anlatim: In the tasks you'll find a page's title, collect all its links, and add up the prices. In the project you're sorting real treasure clues from traps on an old page.
In short: give the HTML to BeautifulSoup, find one with find and all with find_all, then take the text and the attributes.
